scope: P01 and P03 chemistry practical plates plus B11 and B12 biology corrections
generator: Built-in imagegen, one call per plate or edit variant. Some failed drafts were retried.
style: Ink and watercolour matching existing m5x and m6 apparatus plates. No text, labels, numbers, logos, people, hands or faces.
qaSummary: All delivered files have RGBA alpha and a transparent canvas corner. Chemistry and biology plates were viewed on cream at 200 px. Pair views and 50 percent overlays were inspected. Cobalt, burner, iron, magnesium and well-plate pairs are visually aligned at review size. The gel wells run across the black electrode end and the gel has no bands. The swab gap is clear at 200 px.
technicalNotes: Imagegen outputs were resampled onto 2000 px or 2048 px delivery canvases to meet the requested dimensions; native generated detail is lower than the delivery dimensions.
The P01 design specifies magnesium ribbon and ash on the same heatproof mat. Brief 64 also asks for oxide in an evaporating dish, so both ash plates are provided.
The two iron edits match the C3 source canvas dimensions and look aligned in the 50 percent overlays. Check the transition in the scene at playback size before freezing it.
The well plate has six rows and eight columns. The card or tile is visible through each empty well, so coded fills should be drawn over the well opening.

wellCentreGrid.accuracy: Visual centre estimate from the black plate. Confirm against the displayed scene before placing coded fills.

biologyCheck.cattleGrid70px: Red and roan are distinguishable at 70 px wide on the paper background. See brief64-qa/b11-cattle-grid-70px.png.
biologyCheck.cheekSwab: v2 has the swab and tube with no detached specks visible in the gap at 200 px.
biologyCheck.gelTank: v2 shows a row of wells across the black negative end, perpendicular to travel toward the red positive end. No bands are painted.

categoryResearch: The NSW Department of Education CSIS chemical lookup redirects unauthenticated access to staff sign-in. Public CSIS appendices mention cobalt(II) chloride storage but do not give its chemical category. No category has been inferred from related salts.

officialSources.title: NSW Department of Education Chemical Safety in Schools chemical lookup
CSIS Volume 2 appendices, p. 139, cobalt(II) chloride storage

copyCheck: No em dash found in chem-m5-p01.md or chem-m5-p03.md.
